sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Chan Kong-sang (born 7 April 1954), also known as Fang Shilong and known professionally as Jackie Chan and Sing Lung, is a Hong Kong martial artist, actor and filmmaker, known for his slapstick, acrobatic fighting style, comic timing, and innovative stunts, which he typically performs himself.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: With a film career spanning seven decades, he is regarded as one of the most iconic and influential martial artists in the history of cinema.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Films in which he has appeared have grossed over $6 billion worldwide.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Starting as one of the Seven Little Fortunes at the China Drama Academy, where he was trained in acrobatics, martial arts and acting, Chan entered the Hong Kong film industry as a stuntman before making the transition to acting.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: His breakthrough came with the action comedy Snake in the Eagle's Shadow (1978).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He then starred in similar action comedies such as Drunken Master (1978) and The Young Master (1980).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He made his directorial debut with The Fearless Hyena (1979), which was a box office success.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Throughout the 1980s, he was part of the "Three Dragons" along with Sammo Hung and Yuen Biao; the three starred in six Hong Kong films together.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Project A (1983) saw the official formation of the Jackie Chan Stunt Team and established Chan's signature style of elaborate, dangerous stunts combined with martial arts and slapstick humor, a style he further developed in a more modern setting with Wheels on Meals (1984) and Police Story (1985).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Rumble in the Bronx (1995), which had a successful worldwide theatrical run, brought Chan into the North American mainstream.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: By the mid-1990s, he was the most popular action movie star in Eurasia.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Chan gained Hollywood success for portraying Chief Inspector Lee in the American buddy cop action comedy film Rush Hour (1998), a role he reprised in two sequels.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He went on to work both in American and Chinese films, appearing in the Shanghai film series (2000–2003), New Police Story (2004), Rob-B-Hood (2006), Little Big Soldier (2010), Shaolin (2011), and The Shadow's Edge (2025), among others.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The Forbidden Kingdom (2008) marked his first collaboration with fellow martial arts star Jet Li.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He has played martial arts mentor Mr. Han in two Karate Kid films, the 2010 remake The Karate Kid and Karate Kid: Legends (2025).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: For CZ12 (2012), he earned two Guinness World Records for "Most Stunts Performed by a Living Actor" and "Most Credits in One Movie".

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He played against type in Shinjuku Incident (2009) and The Foreigner (2017).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: His voice acting work includes all three Chinese versions of Mulan (1998), the first three films in the Kung Fu Panda franchise (2008–2016), and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem (2023).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: One of the most recognizable and influential film personalities in the world, Chan was described by film scholar Andrew Willis in 2004 as perhaps "the most recognized star in the world."

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He has received fame stars on the Hong Kong Avenue of Stars and the Hollywood Walk of Fame, as well as an honorary Academy Award in 2016.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Chan has been referenced in various pop songs, films, television series, and video games.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He has an award named after him, the Jackie Chan Action Movie Awards.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He is an operatically trained vocalist who has released several pop music albums and performed theme songs for some of the films in which he starred.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He is also a philanthropist and was named one of the top 10 most charitable celebrities by Forbes in 2011.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: In 2016, Forbes ranked him the second-highest-paid actor in the world.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan was born on 7 April 1954 in British Hong Kong as Chan Kong-sang to Charles and Lee-lee Chan, political refugees from the Chinese Civil War.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: In circa 1937, Chan's father, originally named Fang Daolong, briefly worked as a secret agent for Lieutenant General Dai Li, the chief spy in Kuomintang-ruled China.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: For fear of being arrested by the communist government, Chan's father fled to British Hong Kong in the 1940s and changed his surname from Fang to Chan.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan was his wife Chan Lee-lee's surname.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan discovered his father's identity and adopted Fang Shilong (房仕龍) as his Chinese name in the late 1990s, the name he would have been named according to his kin's genealogy book, which allegedly traces back to Tang dynasty statesman Fang Xuanling.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan's ancestral roots are located in Wuhu, Anhui.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan spent his formative years within the grounds of the French consul's residence in the Victoria Peak, British Hong Kong, as his father worked as a cook there.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan attended the Nah-Hwa Primary School on Hong Kong Island, where he failed his first year, after which his parents withdrew him from the school.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: In 1960, his father emigrated to Canberra, Australia to work as the head cook for the American embassy, and Chan was sent to the China Drama Academy, a Peking Opera School run by Master Yu Jim-yuen.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan trained rigorously for the next decade, excelling in martial arts and acrobatics.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: He eventually became part of the Seven Little Fortunes, a performance group made up of the school's best students, gaining the stage name Yuen Lo (元樓) in homage to his master.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan became close friends with fellow group members Sammo Hung and Yuen Biao, and the three of them later became known as the Three Brothers or Three Dragons.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: After entering the film industry, Chan along with Sammo Hung got the opportunity to train in hapkido under the grand master Jin Pal Kim, and Chan eventually attained a black belt.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: As a martial artist, Chan is also skilled in multiple forms of Kung fu.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: He is also known to have trained in other martial art forms such as Karate, Judo, Boxing, Taekwondo, and Jeet Kune Do.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Chan joined his parents in Canberra, Australia in 1971, where he briefly attended Dickson College and worked as a construction worker.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: A fellow builder named Jack took Chan under his wing, thus earning Chan the nickname of "Little Jack", later shortened to "Jacky".

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: In the 1980s, the spelling of his nickname became "Jackie", which has stuck with him ever since.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: A spokesman later said Chan was referring to freedom in the entertainment industry, rather than in Chinese society at large.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In December 2012, Chan caused outrage when he criticized Hong Kong as a "city of protest", suggesting that demonstrators' rights in Hong Kong should be limited.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: The same month, in an interview with Phoenix TV, Chan stated that the United States was the "most corrupt" country in the world, which in turn angered parts of the online community.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Other articles situated Chan's comments in the context of his career and life in the United States, including his "embrace of the American film market" and his seeking asylum in the United States from Hong Kong triads.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: From 2013 to 2023, Chan served two terms as a member of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, representing the "Literature and Arts" sector.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In April 2016, Chan was named in the Panama Papers.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: While Chan was not accused of engaging in illegal activity, he was listed as having up to six different offshore accounts, likely for the purposes of serving as tax shelters.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In 2019, Chan criticized Hong Kong anti-extradition bill protests, saying that the Five-starred Red Flag' is respected everywhere around the world."

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: He also supported the National People's Congress decision on Hong Kong national security legislation.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In addition to his film production and distribution company, JCE Movies Limited, Jackie Chan owns or co-owns the production companies JC Group China, Jackie & Willie Productions (with Willie Chan) and Jackie & JJ Productions.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Chan has also put his name to Jackie Chan Theater International, a cinema chain in China, co-run by Hong Kong company Sparkle Roll Group Ltd. The first—Jackie Chan-Yaolai International Cinema—opened in February 2010, and is claimed to be the largest cinema complex in China, with 17 screens and 3,500 seats.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Chan expressed his hopes that the size of the venue would afford young, non-commercial directors the opportunity to have their films screened.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Fifteen further cinemas in the chain were planned for 2010, throughout Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou, with a potential total of 65 cinemas throughout the country proposed.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In 2004, Chan launched his own line of clothing, which bears a Chinese dragon logo and the English word "Jackie", or the initials "JC".

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Chan also has a number of other branded businesses.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: His sushi restaurant chain, Jackie's Kitchen, has outlets throughout Hong Kong, as well as seven in South Korea, with plans to open another in Las Vegas.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Jackie Chan's Cafe has outlets in Beijing, Singapore, and the Philippines.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Other ventures include Jackie Chan Signature Club gyms (a partnership with California Fitness), and a line of chocolates, cookies and nutritional oatcakes.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: With each of his businesses, a percentage of the profits goes to various charities, including the Jackie Chan Charitable Foundation.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In 2016, Chan partnered with Asian Le Mans Series champion David Cheng to form a racing team in the series and the FIA World Endurance Championship.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: The two met in March 2015 and Chan told Cheng about his interest in motorsports and raised the possibility of starting a team.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Together, the two formed Baxi DC Racing Alpine, the first mainland China-based operation in WEC.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In October, leading into the 2016–17 Asian Le Mans Series season, the team was rebranded to Jackie Chan DC Racing and raced with liveries promoting Chan's movie Kung Fu Yoga.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: At the 2017 24 Hours of Le Mans, the team became the first Chinese team to win its class (LMP2).

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Chan is a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador, and has championed charitable works and causes.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: He has campaigned for conservation and against animal abuse, and has promoted disaster relief efforts for floods in mainland China and the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In June 2006, citing his admiration of the efforts made by Warren Buffett and Bill Gates to help those in need, Chan pledged the donation of half his assets to charity upon his death.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: On 10 March 2008, Chan was the guest of honour for the launch, by Australian Prime Minister Kevin Rudd, of the Jackie Chan Science Centre at the John Curtin School of Medical Research of the Australian National University.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Chan is also a supporter and ambassador of Save China's Tigers, which aims to save the endangered South China tiger through breeding and releasing them into the wild.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Following the 2008 Sichuan earthquake, Chan donated RMB ¥10 million to help those in need.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In addition, he planned to make a film about the Chinese earthquake to raise money for survivors.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In response to the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, Chan and fellow Hong Kong-based celebrities, including American rapper MC Jin, headlined a special three-hour charity concert, titled Artistes 311 Love Beyond Borders, on 1 April 2011 to help with Japan's disaster recovery effort.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: The 3-hour concert raised over $3.3 million.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In January 2017, Chan donated $65,000 to help flood victims in Thailand.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: Chan founded the Jackie Chan Charitable Foundation in 1988 to offer scholarship and active help to Hong Kong's young people and provide aid to victims of natural disaster or illness.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In 2005, Chan created the Dragon's Heart Foundation to help children and the elderly in remote areas of China by building schools, providing books, fees, and uniforms for children; the organisation expanded its reach to Europe in 2011.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: The foundation also provides for the elderly with donations of warm clothing, wheelchairs, and other items.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In the 1990s, Chan bought 10 antique sandalwood buildings, aged 200-400 years old, from Anhui province with the intention for his parents to live in upon completion of their renovation.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: His parents died before the renovation works in Suzhou was be completed and he had them stored in warehouses.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In 2009, Chan donated 4 of these buildings to the Singapore government which made arrangements to have them restore in the campus of Singapore University of Technology and Design.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In 2013, Chan stated his intentions to donated the remaining houses to Singapore after he failed to reach an agreement with the Hong Kong government to have them publicly accessible.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: This intention sparked a debate within China that such historic buildings should remained within the country, however, there was acknowledgement that such structures had a better chance of being preserved outside of the country.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: One product which Chan had endorsed in China was the "Little Tyrant" ("小霸王") produced by Subor, a Nintendo Entertainment System hardware clone marketed as a "learning machine" to circumvent China's then-ban on video game consoles.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In 2010, Chan served as brand ambassador for Kaspersky Lab's antivirus software in Asia.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: There is an urban legend called the Jackie Chan curse.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: ABC News reported in 2010 that the legend originated because "A slew of products sold in China bearing his name, smile and seal of approval have proven defective, prone to explosion, and in one case, potentially damaging to consumers' health."

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: This led to a belief that any product or company which was endorsed by Jackie Chan would suffer setbacks.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: In 2016 the failure of fitness chain California Fitness was blamed on the curse.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: The curse was again invoked in 2021 when Evergrande Group suffered major losses following Chan's promotion of Evergrande Spring brand bottled water.

sentences.section: 1988–1998: Acclaimed film sequels and Hollywood breakthrough
sentences.text: However, Jackie Chan has also endorsed a number of products and companies which have not had issues.
